question: What is the typical average length of a complete ovarian cycle?
explanation: A standard text-book ovarian cycle is calculated to last about twenty-eight days, though normal variations among women are very common. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: What are the two primary functions of the ovaries during this monthly cycle?

options.A: Maturing follicles and producing sex hormones
options.B: Digesting fats and making red blood cells
options.C: Producing urine and filtering blood cells
options.D: Storing waste and regulating body temperature

explanation: The ovaries have a dual role of developing the female gametes inside follicles and secreting vital hormones like estrogen and progesterone. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the name of the mature, fluid-filled follicle ready for release?
explanation: The Graafian follicle is the final, large, fluid-filled stage of follicular development that ruptures during ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why do many follicles start growing at first, but usually only one reaches full maturity?

options.A: Only one ovary is allowed to work at a time
options.B: The body destroys all follicles except the very smallest one
options.C: One dominant follicle hogs the available supply of stimulating hormones
options.D: Infections wipe out the rest of the growing eggs

explanation: Think of it as a competition! The dominant follicle grabs the most hormonal support, causing the others to stop growing and fade away. You're doing great learning this!

question: Which brain structure releases gonadotropin-releasing hormone to start the cycle?
explanation: The hypothalamus is the master control center that secretes gonadotropin-releasing hormone to trigger the pituitary gland. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h3)

question: How do the ovaries communicate back to the brain about their hormone levels?

options.A: By altering the physical size of the pituitary gland
options.B: By sending electrical impulses down the spinal cord
options.C: By sending estrogen and progesterone through the blood
options.D: By releasing white blood cells into lymphatic channels

explanation: Ovarian hormones travel through the bloodstream to send feedback signals back to the brain (the hypothalamus and pituitary gland). Simple and amazing how the body works!

question: Which specific hormone surge directly triggers the release of the egg from the ovary?
explanation: A sharp peak in luteinizing hormone is the exact physiological trigger that causes the follicle to burst and release the egg. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h4)

question: A patient is tracking her ovulation using an over-the-counter urine test kit. Which hormone is the kit primarily designed to detect?
explanation: Home ovulation prediction kits detect the sudden surge of luteinizing hormone that happens twenty-four to thirty-six hours before ovulation. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h4)

question: What does the ruptured follicle turn into after ovulation occurs?
explanation: The leftover follicular cells change structurally and functionally to become the hormone-secreting corpus luteum. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the primary hormonal job of the corpus luteum during the second half of the cycle?

options.A: Lowering body temperature to prevent fevers
options.B: Producing large amounts of follicle-stimulating hormone
options.C: Triggering the immediate shedding of the uterine wall
options.D: Secreting high levels of progesterone to maintain the womb lining

explanation: Progesterone released by the corpus luteum prepares and maintains the endometrium for a possible pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h5)

question: What hormone must be released by a developing embryo to keep the corpus luteum alive?
explanation: Embryonic human chorionic gonadotropin signals the corpus luteum not to degenerate, ensuring continued hormone support for the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h6)

question: What happens when fertilization does NOT take place during the cycle?

options.A: Progesterone drops and the uterine lining sheds
options.B: Progesterone rises and the uterine lining thickens further
options.C: Estrogen disappears completely and ovulation happens again
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin spikes in the blood

explanation: When pregnancy doesn't happen, the corpus luteum fades, progesterone levels fall, and the body sheds the uterine lining as a menstrual period. Totally normal physiology!

question: Which of the following is NOT a common cause of disrupted ovarian cycles?

options.C: Extreme weight loss or eating disorders

explanation: Normal fluid intake supports health but does not disrupt the delicate hormonal axis that controls ovulation, unlike severe stress, weight loss, or disease states. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h7)

question: A patient presents with irregular periods, excess facial hair, and trouble conceiving due to missing ovulation. Which condition does this suggest?

options.A: Normal variant of a short cycle

explanation: Polycystic ovary syndrome is characterized by anovulation, high androgen levels, and irregular menstrual cycles. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T3#GNS216_U2_T3_h7)
